structure: Part 5, Origin and arrival status. Read in full, at repo HEAD 2f2b07f: every file of journeys/linear/features/origin/ (evaluation.js, page.js, controller.js, template.njk, controller.test.js, origin.fit.spec.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js) and every file of journeys/linear/features/arrival-status/ (evaluation.js, page.js, controller.js, template.njk, statuses.js, controller.test.js, arrival-status.fit.spec.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js), plus obligations/sections/origin.js, obligations/sections/arrival.js and shared/kit.js for context only (parts 12 and 13 claim them). Since the earlier extract (a88175f) only the two controller tests' backend-failure helper and kit.js's stale-concurrency and save-fallback logging changed; no page, copy or rule in this slice moved. Covered: the origin page (route, heading, caption, the one country type-ahead over a native select and its configuration, select text, placeholder, no-results text, required and membership rule, the three per-category narrowing rules and their messages, territory-to-parent-country matching, the ware-potato guidance inset, the stale saved country state, save controls, Back link, redirects, save failures); the arrival-status page (route, legend as h1, caption, the two statuses with labels and hints, the 4-day window in the post-arrival hint, the required rule, Save and return refusals, redirects, save failures); the scope rule that skips arrival status for potatoes and what a potato notifier sees instead; every English and Welsh copy key in both features; all 19 tests of origin.fit.spec.js and all 18 of arrival-status.fit.spec.js; both evaluation.js bindings as mechanism claims.

claims.statement: The Welsh arrival-status question is 'Ydy’r llwyth wedi cyrraedd Prydain Fawr?', used as both title and legend, with Great Britain translated as 'Prydain Fawr'.
claims.quote:
title: 'Ydy’r llwyth wedi cyrraedd Prydain Fawr?',
  legend: 'Ydy’r llwyth wedi cyrraedd Prydain Fawr?',

claims.statement: The Welsh arrival-status answers are labelled 'Ydy, mae wedi cyrraedd yn barod' and 'Nac ydy, nid yw wedi cyrraedd eto'.

The Welsh arrival-status hints are 'Rydych yn gwneud hysbysiad ar ôl cyrraedd. Rhaid ei wneud heb fod yn hwyrach na ${days} diwrnod ar ôl y dyddiad cyrraedd. Byddwch yn rhoi’r dyddiad y cyrhaeddodd a ble mae nawr.' for already arrived and 'Rydych yn gwneud hysbysiad cyn cyrraedd. Byddwch yn rhoi’r dyddiad glanio disgwyliedig a’r cyrchfan arfaethedig.' for not yet arrived.
claims.quote:
'already-arrived': (days) =>
      `Rydych yn gwneud hysbysiad ar ôl cyrraedd. Rhaid ei wneud heb fod yn hwyrach na ${days} diwrnod ar ôl y dyddiad cyrraedd. Byddwch yn rhoi’r dyddiad y cyrhaeddodd a ble mae nawr.`,

claims.statement: The Welsh arrival-status required error is 'Dewiswch a yw’r llwyth wedi cyrraedd'.

The English wording of the arrival-status page is itself provisional and awaiting a copy pass, and its Welsh is machine drafted with no source sentence behind any leaf, so neither may be shown to a user as settled.
The English and Welsh arrival-status bundles hold the same keys at every leaf.
claims.quote: itHoldsCopyAtEveryLeaf(copy, cy)

claims.statement: The arrival-status page states the 4-day post-arrival window as guidance but nothing on it, or on the origin page, refuses a notification made later than that window.
claims.ref: journeys/linear/features/arrival-status/ and features/origin/ (every file read; the only use of PLANTS_WOOD_DAYS_AFTER_ARRIVAL is the hint at arrival-status/controller.js:35-38)
claims.note: Looked in both controllers, both templates, both copy bundles and all four test files: the window appears only inside the hint sentence. Whether the window is enforced, and where, is not shown in this part; the arrival date page is part 6's.

claims.statement: Two of the three origin narrowing rules are never stated to the notifier before they answer: only the ware-potato rule has an inset, so a notifier of conifer wood without bark, or of plants and wood generally, learns the rule only by being refused. Inferred because the guidance block holds one key and the page builds its insets only from constraints that have one.
claims.note: The guidance list is built only from constraints that have a guidance string, so the other two constraints contribute nothing to the page.

claims.statement: The origin page's stale-saved-country state is proven only by unit tests; no end-to-end test in this part shows a notifier being told their saved country is no longer available.
claims.ref: journeys/linear/features/origin/origin.fit.spec.js (all 19 tests read; none names countryNoLongerAvailable) against controller.test.js:123-161
claims.note: Searched the whole fit spec for the copy key and for the message text: neither appears. The unit suite covers the state in four tests.

claims.statement: A saved country the service no longer offers is listed in the error summary as well as on the field when the origin page opens, because the page builds its error summary from the same errors it shows on the field.
claims.quote: errorSummary: kit.errorSummary(errors),
claims.note: No test asserts the summary in the stale-country state; controller.test.js:143-151 asserts only the field error.

claims.statement: The narrowing of origin countries by commodity line is checked on the origin page itself, not by the obligation's scope rules, because a line's category sits below the notification-level answer an obligation gate reads.
claims.ref: obligations/sections/origin.js:5-9 (read for context; part 12 claims the obligation)
claims.quote:
so the narrowing is validated on the page

claims.statement: A notification started straight at the origin page in the fit suite goes from origin to the arrival details, not to the arrival-status question, so the suite's default start-at-origin notification is one the question does not apply to.
claims.note: Inferred from where Save and continue lands; startNotificationAtOrigin lives in fit/high-risk-plants-journey.js, outside this part, so the commodity type it seeds is not shown here.
